bilingual.notes: Bilingual-Bicultural Education (subject 1023) is a supplemental license under PI 34.078 — it requires an underlying Tier II/III/IV teaching license and is not standalone. PI 34.078(2)(b) requires proficiency in English and the target language; PI 34.078(2)(c) requires an approved program with coursework in cultural studies, foundations, theory and methodology, contrastive language study (phonology/morphology/syntax), bilingual-bicultural field experiences, and a clinical program. No state-adopted bilingual content test exists; each EPP measures English and target-language proficiency (commonly via ACTFL). The underlying primary-license content test and edTPA gate the pathway.

eld.notes: ESL (subject 1395) is a kindergarten through grade 12 teaching-area license under PI 34.047(3)(e) earned via an approved program plus assessments under PI 34.021(1)(c)-(d) (Praxis II ESOL #0360, passing 530, plus edTPA in Teaching Students of Other Languages). PI 34.052(6) creates an add-on pathway for holders of an elementary/middle school, special education, or equivalent license: the ESL credential may be added by passing the approved content knowledge test (no second approved program required). No language-proficiency exam is required of ESL candidates.

sei.notes: Wisconsin does not mandate SEI-style training for all teachers. SEI/Sheltered English/Content-Based ESL is one of several Language Instruction Educational Program models (alongside pull-out ESL, push-in ESL, and bilingual program models) districts may run, taught by ESL-licensed (1395) staff.

history.title: Wisconsin Bilingual-Bicultural Education Act enacted (Ch. 395, Laws of 1975)
history.description: Wisconsin enacted one of the strongest state bilingual mandates in the country, codified at Wis. Stat. §§ 115.95 to 115.996. Districts must operate a bilingual-bicultural education program at any school enrolling 10 or more EL students at the K-3 level, 20 or more at grades 4-8, or 20 or more at the high-school level — all of the same non-English language background. The 1975 act also established the bilingual-bicultural teacher license category that PI 34.078 (formerly PI 34.33(3)) administers today, and is the legal source of Wisconsin's status as a bilingual-program state rather than an SEI state. The statute's combination with WIDA (headquartered at UW-Madison) makes Wisconsin distinctive in the upper Midwest.

history.title: Wisconsin Seal of Biliteracy initiated by DPI
history.description: DPI launched the Wisconsin Seal of Biliteracy in October 2015 to recognize graduating high-school students who demonstrate proficiency in English plus one or more additional languages. The program is administered by DPI rather than created by a standalone authorizing statute; districts opt in and award the seal locally.

history.title: DPI publishes ESL/Bilingual-Bicultural/World Languages license guidance
history.description: DPI's Teacher Education, Professional Development and Licensing team issued a one-stop guidance document mapping each WI language-instruction license (ESL 1395, Bilingual-Bicultural 1023, World Language) to the program models it can be used in (sheltered/SEI, pull-out/push-in ESL, transitional/two-way/maintenance bilingual, immersion) and the educator-preparation requirements for each — including Praxis II ESOL #0360 (passing 530), edTPA, and the EPP-administered language-proficiency check (commonly ACTFL) for bilingual candidates.

history.title: Chapter PI 34 (educator licenses) reorganized and renumbered
history.description: The Wisconsin administrative-rule re-number consolidated the educator licensing scheme. The bilingual-bicultural supplemental rule moved from PI 34.33(3) to PI 34.078; the ESL teaching-area subject moved from PI 34.30(g) to PI 34.047(3)(e); and the add-on-by-content-test pathway for ESL/world-languages was placed at PI 34.052(6). Substantive requirements (approved program, English + target-language proficiency for bilingual, content-area test for add-on) were preserved across the renumbering.

history.title: Refresh against current SEA sources (verified-2026)
history.description: Re-verified Wisconsin's record against current DPI pages and Wisconsin Administrative Code Chapter PI 34. Corrections vs. baseline: bilingual is supplemental (not standalone) under PI 34.078; ESL is available both as a standalone PI 34.047(3)(e) license and as a PI 34.052(6) content-test add-on; the operative 10 Wisconsin Educator Standards do not literally mention 'linguistic' or 'English learner,' so those professionalStandardsMentions booleans flip to false; elPercent updated to 5.9% (NCES Fall 2021).
